title: Ali's death
hookLine: Ali is struck in the mosque at Kufa during Ramadan, and asks that his killer be treated fairly (reported)

cards: It is Ramadan, still dark, and people are coming into the mosque at Kufa for the dawn prayer. Ali, the caliph, is among them. So is a man named Ibn Muljam, and he has a sword.
He is one of the Kharijites, the ones who declared Ali an unbeliever for agreeing to talk at Siffin. Umar fell at this same hour, in Medina. Now Ibn Muljam strikes Ali on the head.
The wound is deep, and Ali is carried home. What he says in the days that follow is the reason this lesson exists.

teach.h: I HAVE WON, BY THE LORD OF THE KA'BAH.
teach.b: Reports say that when he was struck, Ali said: by the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won. Shia and Sunni sources both carry versions of this: a man struck down at prayer, in the month of fasting, counting it as victory.
Then come his instructions about the man who did it. The histories, and the letter of counsel to his sons Hasan and Husayn kept in Nahj al-Balagha, give them like this.
Keep him well. Feed him, and give him somewhere decent to stay. If I live, I will decide what to do with him; I may forgive him.

teach.h: ONE BLOW FOR ONE BLOW, NO MORE.
teach.b: If I die, then one blow for one blow. Do not kill anyone else on my account. And do not mutilate him, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, forbade mutilation, even of a rabid dog.

Set that against the times: a city in turmoil, a ruler struck by a man who called him an unbeliever, and the dying man's worry is that his own side might go too far. No mob, no revenge on a whole tribe.
Only what the law allows, with forgiveness left open. Ali died of the wound soon after. Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth rightly guided caliph.
Shia Muslims mourn him as the first Imam, and observe the nights of his wounding and his death in Ramadan with prayer and grief.
His shrine at Najaf, in Iraq, is where Shia Muslims hold he is buried, and pilgrims go there. The fitnah was not over, but this is how Ali left it.

how: Shia Muslims mourn Ali's wounding and death on nights of Ramadan with prayer and gatherings and visit his shrine at Najaf; Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth rightly guided caliph and retell his instructions about his killer.

struck at prayer, he asked fair treatment for his killer

games.q: you're Ali, badly wounded. your sons ask what to do with the man who struck you. what do you tell them?
o: feed him, keep him well, and if I die, one blow for one, no more.
games.why: the reports say he asked them to keep him well, forbade mutilation, and limited any punishment to the killer alone.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has truly wronged you, and notice what you'd like to happen to them. Ask Ali's narrower question: what would be fair, and no more?
Let go of the extra blow, the story told to everyone; if you pray, you can leave the rest with God.

wordCard.voice: Ali's death. Struck at the dawn prayer in Kufa, in Ramadan, by a Kharijite, he asked, the reports say, that his killer be kept well and treated within the law, and no further. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: by the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won; words reported from Ali when he was struck.

carryVoice: Your line: fair to his killer. Justice, and not one blow more. That's day eight hundred eighty-six.
